Micron Taoyuan union secures strike authorization, weighs 'surprise strike'

Taipei, Oct. 7 (CNA) The union representing workers at U.S. memory chipmaker Micron Technology Inc.'s operations in Taoyuan said Wednesday it had secured authorization to strike and was considering a "surprise strike" if talks with the company fail to produce results.

Of 2,258 eligible union members, 2,012 voted over the past six days, with 1,994 supporting strike action, 14 opposed and four invalid ballots.

The result meant 88.3 percent of all eligible members backed a strike, or 99 percent of those who voted.

Speaking at a news conference in Taipei, Jerry Lin (林哲瑞), the union's chairman, said no strike date had been set.

"We haven't decided on an actual strike schedule yet, but when the time comes, we will notify members by text message," Lin said, adding that a "surprise strike" was among the options being considered.

Asked later about the option, Lin said the union could announce a strike at short notice "to prevent the company from making preparations in advance."

The union said it hoped Micron's board would offer concrete proposals after a meeting scheduled for Oct. 8-9 U.S. time, before further action is taken.
